questions.question: Q: How did the Roman Republic balance different elements of government?
questions.correctAnswer: Consuls provided monarchical executive power (but there were two, each vetoing the other). The Senate provided aristocratic guidance and expertise. The assemblies provided democratic participation. This mixed constitution was admired by later political thinkers including Polybius.

questions.question: Q: What powers did the Senate hold?
questions.correctAnswer: The Senate controlled foreign policy (declaring war, making treaties), managed state finances, supervised the treasury, appointed provincial governors, and issued decrees (senatus consulta) that were effectively law. Its 300 members served for life, giving it institutional memory and immense authority.

questions.question: Q: Why were tribunes of the plebs important?
questions.correctAnswer: Tribunes were the plebeians' protection against patrician oppression. They could veto any magistrate's action, convene the plebeian assembly, propose laws, and their persons were sacrosanct (inviolable). They were the primary mechanism through which plebeians gained political rights over time.

questions.question: Q: What was the cursus honorum?
questions.correctAnswer: The prescribed sequence of political offices: quaestor (financial administrator, minimum age 30), aedile (public works and games), praetor (judicial and military command, minimum age 39), and consul (chief magistrate, minimum age 42). Two-year intervals between offices were required.

questions.question: Q: When and why was a dictator appointed?
questions.correctAnswer: In extreme emergencies (military crisis or internal disorder), a dictator was appointed by the consuls for a maximum of six months with supreme authority. All other magistrates were subordinate to the dictator. The most famous example is Cincinnatus, who was appointed, defeated the enemy, and resigned after just 16 days.
